View Test Case
Preconditions
Staging environment selected. Collection variables cleared.
Steps
  1. 1. POST V1 Search (api/FlightSearch/Search) with the above body. 2. POST V2 Search (api/V2/FlightSearch/Search) with the same criteria. 3. Record offers count, canBeHeld, haveBundles and offerHasAncillary per offer.
Expected Result
HTTP 200 on both versions with non-empty offers[]; no 'credentials ... do not exist or are not active' error. canBeHeld=true expected (baseline 67/67) so Hold-based cases are runnable; haveBundles=false expected so Bundle+Void flows are out of scope.
Actual Result
Both versions 200 with 53 offers. canBeHeld 53/53 (Hold cases runnable), haveBundles 0/53 (Bundle+Void flows out of scope). Baseline was 67 offers on 2026-08-05; the count differs because the date and the live inventory differ. V2 offerHasAncillary is now true on 25 offers (SPEC 4.6 Ancillary cell was Conditional), so an ANC + Void flow could now be scheduled; V1 Search does not return that flag at all.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Staging environment selected.
Steps
  1. 1. POST V2 Search once per selector. 2. Record 200 with offers, or the credentials error text, per selector.
Expected Result
UAE active (baseline). For EGY and KSA record active/inactive. Inactive selectors return the 'credentials for the selected supplier do not exist or are not active' 400 ValidationError.
Actual Result
UAE active, EGY ACTIVE (48 offers), KSA inactive with the documented credentials 400. NEG-04 therefore uses KSA as the inactive selector; EGY is an active second selector, so SEC-03(b) is runnable.
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-02 - [Response] Verify a TravelportNdc Book returns synchronously issued ticket numbers and records the voidCapability value.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Book a TravelportNdc flight and check it shows whether it can be voided
Request: Booked one adult Cairo to Jeddah on 12 Nov 2026 on each API version, then looked each booking up
Response: Both bookings were ticketed at once (V1 72HIJQ, V2 72HZA2), but neither the booking nor the lookup says whether a void is allowed
Expected: The booking should be ticketed and should carry a flag saying whether a void is allowed
Actual: Failed: tickets are issued, but the void-eligibility flag (voidCapability) is missing on both versions
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Key lists of both Book bodies contain no voidCapability; Retrieve (V1 and V2) also lacks it. tickets is an object map keyed travelerRefId_N, not an array

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 passed with canBeHeld=true on the chosen offer (TravelportNdc Hold = Supported, confirmed live 2026-08-05).
Steps
  1. 1. Search -> FareConfirm -> (V2: AddPassenger ->) Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. 2. Confirm tickets[] populated and record voidCapability. 3. POST Void the same day. 4. Record response.
Expected Result
HTTP 2xx with the same success shape as POS-01/02 (per version). pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken unchanged since Hold (same-PNR invariant), and Void behaves identically for a booking that started as a Hold.
Actual Result
V2: Void succeeds for a booking that started as a Hold, with the same success shape as POS-02; pnr, gdsPNR and bookingToken are unchanged from Hold through BookAfterHold and Void (same-PNR invariant holds). Timestamps: Hold response received 11:13:33Z, BookAfterHold ticketingDate 2026-10-26T11:14:09 (the void window is measured from this ticketing time, not from the Hold), Void sent at 11:14:xx the same day; the Hold carries no creation date field. V1: the Hold and BookAfterHold hops work but Void is refused with 409 OperationNotSupported (see TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03), so the V1 ticket 1572141427323 was left live and voided later through the V2 endpoint during cleanup. Verdict follows V2.
TC-VOIDTPN-POS-04 - [Response] Verify Void of a multi-passenger TravelportNdc booking (ADT+CHD+INF) voids every ticket on the PNR.PASS
Endpoint Name: Void a booking with an adult, a child and an infant
Request: Booked three tickets and voided with an empty ticket list
Response: All three tickets were voided in one call on version 2
Expected: Every ticket on the booking, including the infant ticket, should be voided
Actual: Passed on version 2 (version 1 still cannot void)
Status: PASS
Evidence
Ticket numbers voided: 1572141427284, 1572141427283, 1572141427285 = the 3 tickets from Book

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Booking ticketed today with one ticket per passenger.
Steps
  1. 1. Book a 3-passenger TravelportNdc booking; record every ticket number. 2. POST Void with voidTickets=[]. 3. Retrieve the PNR.
Expected Result
Void succeeds; voidedTickets lists all 3 tickets (including the infant ticket); Retrieve shows every ticket in a voided state - none left active. Exact voided-state signal UNKNOWN (see TC-VOIDTPN-INT-02).
Actual Result
V2: voidTickets=[] means void-all: all 3 tickets including the infant ticket are voided and the PNR is cancelled, none left active. The per-ticket voided state cannot be read back afterwards because Retrieve of a voided PNR returns the terminal 409 (INT-02). V1: refused (409 OperationNotSupported); the V1 booking was voided via V2 during cleanup.

Response: Version 2 voided all three; plain numbers or strings were refused with a clear 400
Expected: Listing all tickets should void the whole booking, same as an empty list
Actual: Passed on version 2 (version 1 still cannot void)
Status: PASS

Element shape = TicketType object (same as SabreNdc, 2026-10-22)

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Multi-passenger booking ticketed today.
Steps
  1. 1. Book; collect all ticket numbers. 2. POST Void with voidTickets=[all ticket numbers]. 3. Retrieve.
Expected Result
Behaves identically to voidTickets=[] (all tickets voided). Record the accepted element shape of voidTickets (plain string vs object) - SPEC §2.15 marks it UNKNOWN.

Accepted element shape recorded: an OBJECT {ticketNumber, carrierCode, ticketStatus}; plain strings and numbers are rejected with a 400 that names $.voidTickets[0] and not a 500 (the message also leaks the internal type name, see VAL-07). V1: refused as unsupported.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void without pnr. 2. POST Void with pnr=''. 3. Retrieve the real booking.
Expected Result
HTTP 400 with the standard error envelope {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode=ValidationError, ErrorMessage, Context naming pnr}; no 500. Real booking remains ticketed (not voided).
Actual Result
V2: a missing or empty pnr is rejected before reaching Travelport with a 400 naming the PNR; the booking is still ticketed. V1: the request never gets as far as validation, the unsupported-supplier 409 comes first.
TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-02 - [Request] Validate missing or empty bookingToken is rejected.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void without the booking token
Request: Sent the void with the token missing and then blank
Response: Version 2 voided the ticket both times
Expected: The request should be refused and the booking left alone
Actual: Failed: the token is not checked, the ticket was voided
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Retrieve after each Void: 409 NDC-INT-BYP-A0003 "Reservation is already cancelled." (booking consumed; a fresh PNR was booked for the empty-string variant)

TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void without bookingToken. 2. POST Void with bookingToken=''. 3. Retrieve the booking.
Expected Result
HTTP 400 ValidationError in the standard envelope; booking not voided.
Actual Result
The booking token is not validated: a Void with no token, or an empty one, is accepted and cancels the ticket. The booking is found from gdsPNR alone (see BND-01 and NEG-02). Expected a 400 ValidationError naming bookingToken with the booking left ticketed.
TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-03 - [Request] Validate whether gdsPNR is mandatory for TravelportNdc Void (empty string as in the V2 saved example).PASS
Endpoint Name: Void without the airline-system reference (gdsPNR)
Request: Sent the void with that reference blank, then missing
Response: Version 2 refused both: "GdsPnr is required"; the bookings stayed ticketed
Expected: Either refused with a clear 400, or accepted by looking the booking up another way
Actual: Passed on version 2: the reference is mandatory
Status: PASS
Evidence
V2 TransactionIds 5e818017-0f00-4b58-901e-903529cf3d40 (empty) and 80766854-3eda-454b-9227-fe5f9427d863 (omitted)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. The booking has a real non-empty gdsPNR (e.g. H07WD3 style).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with gdsPNR=''. 2. If rejected, POST with gdsPNR omitted. 3. Retrieve the booking after each call.
Expected Result
Confirm live: either (a) rejected with 400 ValidationError naming gdsPNR (mandatory for GDS-routed TravelportNdc), or (b) Void succeeds because the integration resolves the record locator from pnr/bookingToken. A 500 or a generic Travelport fault is a defect. Record which.
Actual Result
Answer to the open SPEC question: gdsPNR IS mandatory for TravelportNdc Void (outcome (a)); an empty or missing value is rejected with a 400 naming GdsPnr, no 500. Unlike SabreNdc (which accepted ""), the saved V2 example with gdsPNR "" cannot be used for TravelportNdc. gdsPNR is also the field the booking is looked up by.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with a wrong surName. 2. POST Void without surName. 3. Retrieve the booking.
Expected Result
Wrong surName: rejected with a 4xx standard envelope, booking not voided (SPEC §2.15 Common Errors). Omitted surName: confirm live whether mandatory for TravelportNdc and record the result.
Actual Result
The passenger-identity check does not exist: a surname that matches no passenger, or no surname at all, voids the ticket. A caller holding only a gdsPNR can void a booking it cannot otherwise identify. Recurrence of the SabreNdc surName defect (2026-10-22) on TravelportNdc.

Status: PASS

Steps

Preconditions
TC-VOIDTPN-POS-01/02 executed.
Steps
  1. 1. Inspect success and failure response bodies field by field. 2. Look for Travelport-native structures (NDC JSON/XML fragments, Travelport error codes, supplierRequest/supplierResponse, credentials, PCC/branch codes, .NET DTO type names such as ...TravelportNdc...Dto).
Expected Result
Success: integration-defined fields only (shape recorded as baseline, same field names and types as the existing contract). Failure: standard envelope {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context}, Status equal to the HTTP code, TransactionId a GUID. No raw Travelport payload, no credentials, no DTO type names in Context.
Actual Result
The success body is clean. Failure bodies are not: the known DTO-name leak is now on TravelportNdc Void, and every supplier-side 409 returns the raw Travelport request and response in the API reply. A scan of those payloads for credentials, PCC/branch codes and passwords found none, but raw supplier internals still reach the caller. (SEC-03(b) additionally shows a Void under the wrong credential set is forwarded to Travelport and refused there.)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Same-day ticketed TravelportNdc booking (reuse one booking for the VAL cases only while Void keeps being rejected).
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void per variant. 2. Retrieve the booking after each call.
Expected Result
Whitespace-only and over-length: HTTP 400 ValidationError, never 500. Case variants: record whether the PNR lookup is case-insensitive; a lowercased real pnr voiding the booking is acceptable only if documented, otherwise note it.
Actual Result
Over-length pnr is correctly rejected with a 400 (never a 500). But a whitespace-only pnr, and every bookingToken variant, are accepted and void the booking: the PNR is only length-checked and the booking is found from gdsPNR, so neither the pnr text nor the token is verified. Lookup is case-insensitive for pnr (lower-cased pnr voids).

Rerun on 2026-10-27 using bookings left from today.

Steps
  1. 1. POST the identical Void again. 2. POST a third time after 30 seconds. 3. Retrieve.
Expected Result
Second Void rejected with a 4xx standard envelope (already voided; exact code UNKNOWN - record); no 500; booking state unchanged; no duplicate voided entries.

A repeat Void is rejected with a 4xx standard envelope (not a second 200, unlike SabreNdc 2026-10-22), no 500, no duplicate voided entries; Void is not idempotent (it does not return a 2xx no-op). The rejection comes from Travelport and the raw supplier reply is echoed in the envelope (VAL-07).

        }

View Test Case
Preconditions
Hold succeeded (tickets[] empty, holdExpirationDate set).
Steps
  1. 1. Search -> FareConfirm -> (V2: AddPassenger ->) Hold. 2. POST Void. 3. Retrieve. 4. Clean up with CancelAfterHold.
Expected Result
Void rejected as not eligible (no tickets) in the standard envelope; booking stays held. If Void cancels the hold instead, record it as a behavior to confirm with the team (CancelAfterHold is the documented path for holds, §2.14).
Actual Result
A Void on a held, unticketed booking is NOT rejected: it returns HTTP 200 with voided:false and, as a side effect, cancels the hold at Travelport. A success status for a void that did nothing, plus a destroyed hold, is the "Void cancels the hold instead" outcome the case asks to flag. CancelAfterHold is the documented path for holds.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Those cases executed.
Steps
  1. 1. Compare voidCapability before each Void with the Void result. 2. Compare voidCapability after a successful Void.
Expected Result
Allowed value before same-day Void -> Void succeeded; VoidNotAllowed (or equivalent) on an aged ticket -> Void rejected; after a successful Void, voidCapability no longer reports void allowed. Any disagreement between flag and outcome is a defect. A field that is absent everywhere is itself a recurrence of the missing-voidCapability defect.
Actual Result
The flag cannot be compared with the outcome because it is never returned; there is no signal at all that a same-day ticket may be voided, nor that a V1 Void is unsupported. A field that is absent everywhere is itself a recurrence of the missing-voidCapability defect (TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-02).

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. 3-ticket booking ticketed today.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void with voidTickets=[one ticket]. 2. Retrieve and compare each ticket's ticketStatus.
Expected Result
Either (a) only the listed ticket is voided and the others stay Booked, with voidedTickets listing exactly one entry, or (b) the request is rejected with a 4xx stating partial void is unsupported. Silently voiding all tickets, or voiding none while returning voided=true, is a defect.
Actual Result
A per-ticket void is not supported and not rejected: naming one ticket silently voids every ticket on the PNR (the infant ticket included), and the response does not say the request was widened. Expected either only the listed ticket voided or a 4xx stating partial void is unsupported.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two ticketed TravelportNdc bookings today.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void on A with variant (a). 2. Retrieve A. 3. POST Void on A with variant (b). 4. Retrieve A and B.
Expected Result
Both rejected with a 4xx standard envelope; A's and B's tickets unchanged. Must not silently void all of A's tickets, and must never void B's ticket.
Actual Result
Neither variant is rejected: the listed ticket is ignored and every ticket on A is voided. B's ticket is never touched (that part is safe). Expected a 4xx for a ticket not on the PNR with A's tickets unchanged, and never a silent void-all.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Those cases executed.
Steps
  1. 1. Tabulate HTTP status, Status, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context per failure. 2. Compare.
Expected Result
Every failure uses {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context}; Status equals the HTTP code; validation errors are 400; business-rule/eligibility errors use one consistent code family. Record the full mapping table for SPEC.md §2.15.
Actual Result
Status always equals the HTTP code and TransactionId is always a GUID, but the failures are not one consistent envelope: two casings (Status/ErrorCode vs status/errorCode "1001"), the unmapped Z9999 whose message is the code itself, the same business condition (reservation cancelled) mapped to two codes depending on carrier (QR BYP-A0003, EK Z9999 with context "ReservationCancelled"), and eligibility errors that reuse generic validation or supplier codes instead of a Void-specific family. Same pattern as SabreNdc BUG-07.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A ticketed TravelportNdc (UAE) booking today. SabreNdc/EGY active.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Void variant (a). 2. POST Void variant (b). 3. Retrieve with TravelportNdc/UAE.
Expected Result
Both rejected (cross-tenant access denied or booking not found); booking still ticketed.
Actual Result
Both cross-credential voids are rejected and the booking stays ticketed, so no cross-tenant void is possible. Two observations: (a) the Void is routed by the supplier named in the request, so a TravelportNdc PNR sent as SabreNdc is looked up in Sabre (not found); (b) the integration does not check ownership itself: with the EGY credentials it forwarded a refund request to Travelport and relied on Travelport to refuse it. Both rejections expose the raw supplier reply (VAL-07).

Actual: Failed: the surname is accepted whatever it contains

View Test Case
Preconditions
Void succeeded.
Steps
  1. 1. POST Retrieve (V1 RetrieveBooking / V2 Retrieve) immediately after Void. 2. Record status, tickets[].ticketStatus, voidCapability, and any status field.
Expected Result
Booking shows as voided: tickets[].ticketStatus changed from Booked to a voided value and voidCapability no longer allows void - or a terminal 409 like cancelled PNRs. Exact signal UNKNOWN (bookingStatus does not exist in V1 Retrieve, §2.11, confirmed on TravelportNdc 2026-08-05) - record it as the baseline. Unchanged Booked tickets = defect.
Actual Result
Baseline recorded: after a Void the booking is no longer retrievable and Retrieve returns a terminal 409 like cancelled PNRs (the same signal as a cancelled hold), not a voided ticketStatus or a bookingStatus value (V1 has no bookingStatus, V2 Retrieve cannot show it). The unchanged-Booked case is only seen on V1, where the Void was refused. The error code differs by carrier (QR BYP-A0003, EK Z9999), tracked in NEG-05.

View Test Case
Preconditions
SabreNdc/EGY active. Baseline: Void returns {voided, voidedTickets[]} in ~10s (2026-10-22).
Steps
  1. 1. Book with SabreNdc/EGY (V2 or V1). 2. POST Void. 3. Compare the response shape with the 2026-10-22 baseline.
Expected Result
HTTP 200 with the same shape as the baseline; unchanged behavior for SabreNdc and for any other supplier that still lacks Void (those keep returning 409 OperationNotSupported).
Actual Result
SabreNdc Void is unchanged and is not routed to the TravelportNdc handler (same shape and ~10s as the 2026-10-22 baseline); a supplier without Void still returns 409 OperationNotSupported.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Those cases executed on both versions.
Steps
  1. 1. Diff field names, types and status codes between V1 and V2 for the same scenario.
Expected Result
Identical success shape (V2 may add passengersVoidedAncillaries and emdTickets) and identical error codes per scenario; any other difference recorded and raised with the team.
Actual Result
V1 and V2 do not return the same shape: V1 never reaches the Void handler, so its success and business-rule responses are all the unsupported-supplier 409, while V2 returns the real contract. Only the request-binding validations (400 errorCode 1001) are identical.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared (§6.1). Whole flow run without delay on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search (capture searchResponseId, offerId) -> FareConfirm (capture fareConfirmResponseId, selectedOfferId; price reconciliation) -> Book (passengersList, contactsList; capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, tickets, voidCapability) -> Retrieve (tickets[].ticketStatus=Booked) -> Void (supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName, voidTickets=[]) -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop HTTP 200/2xx; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided (signal per TC-VOIDTPN-INT-02). Price reconciliation holds through Book.
Actual Result
Hops 1-4 pass and the price reconciles through Book (1815 AED at Search, FareConfirm and Book). The flow fails at the Void hop: V1 Void is not available for TravelportNdc, so the ticket stays live (voided afterwards through the V2 endpoint during cleanup). Baseline unchanged from 2026-08-05.
FLOW-V1-05-TPN - [Search]&[FareConfirm]&[Hold]&[BookAfterHold]&[Void] [Response] Verify Family-E flow #5 completes end to end for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Whole V1 hold-then-ticket flow ending in a void
Request: Held a seat, repriced it, ticketed it from the hold and tried to void
Response: Everything worked until the void, which was refused as unsupported
Expected: Every step works and the final lookup shows the ticket voided
Actual: Failed at the void step
Status: FAIL
Evidence
ok Search offer reconciles (fully itemized offer picked) (28 of 53 offers fully itemized); ok FareConfirm reconciles; ok FareConfirm total equals Search total (1815 vs 1815); ok Hold selectedOffer reconciles; ok Hold total equals FareConfirm tier total (1815 vs 1815); ok FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) 200; ok BookAfterHold issues tickets; ids unchanged (pnr MQEVZS token same true); ok Retrieve before Void shows tickets Booked (1765766798598:Booked); FAIL Void succeeds (2xx, voided=true) (409 409 {"Status":409,"TransactionId":"8f00169e-45f8-4f62-a33d-3ed38c62b40b","ErrorCode":"OperationNotSupported","ErrorMessa)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen offer. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold (IDs unchanged; tickets populated) -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; BookAfterHold issues tickets; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
Family-E chain works on V1 until the Void hop: the hold is repriced (1815 AED unchanged), ticketed from the hold, and the pnr, gdsPNR and bookingToken stay the same. Void is refused as unsupported, so the ticket stays live (voided later via the V2 endpoint, cleanup).
FLOW-V1-09-TPN - [Search]&[UpSelling]&[Book]&[Retrieve]&[Void] [Response] Verify Family-C flow #9 completes end to end for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Whole V1 upsell flow ending in a void
Request: Searched, upsold, booked and tried to void on version 1
Response: Booking worked at the upsell fare; the void was refused as unsupported
Expected: Every step works and the final lookup shows the ticket voided
Actual: Failed at the void step
Status: FAIL
Evidence
ok Search offer reconciles (fully itemized offer picked) (28 of 53 offers fully itemized); FAIL Upselling returns selectedOffer (documented drop-in for FareConfirm) (keys: responseId,supplier,journeys,flightSegments,priceClasses,baggageDetails,upsellOffers); ok Upselling tier reconciles; ok Book selectedOffer reconciles; ok Book total equals Upselling tier total (1815 vs 1815); ok Retrieve before Void shows tickets Booked (1765766798597:Booked); FAIL Void succeeds (2xx, voided=true) (409 409 {"Status":409,"TransactionId":"4ac805d1-2634-486f-ab6c-267dfe99b4d8","ErrorCode":"OperationNotSupported","ErrorMessa)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling (capture upSellingResponseId and the selected tier's offerId) -> Book (using the upselling ids) -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop succeeds; the booked tier's price matches the Upselling tier; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
The booked fare equals the Upselling tier (1815 AED). Two hops fail their expectation: V1 Upselling returns upsellOffers[] and no selectedOffer, so the documented drop-in for FareConfirm does not hold and the first tier had to be chosen by hand; and the Void hop is refused as unsupported (ticket left live, voided via V2 in cleanup).
FLOW-V1-11-TPN - [Search]&[UpSelling]&[Hold]&[BookAfterHold]&[Void] [Response] Verify Family-E flow #11 completes end to end for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Whole V1 upsell-and-hold flow ending in a void
Request: Upsold, held, repriced, ticketed from the hold and tried to void on version 1
Response: Everything worked until the void, which was refused as unsupported
Expected: Every step works and the final lookup shows the ticket voided
Actual: Failed at the void step
Status: FAIL
Evidence
ok Search offer reconciles (fully itemized offer picked) (28 of 53 offers fully itemized); FAIL Upselling returns selectedOffer (documented drop-in for FareConfirm) (keys: responseId,supplier,journeys,flightSegments,priceClasses,baggageDetails,upsellOffers); ok Upselling tier reconciles; ok Hold selectedOffer reconciles; ok Hold total equals Upselling tier total (1815 vs 1815); ok FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) 200; ok BookAfterHold issues tickets; ids unchanged (pnr MRJVLF token same true); ok Retrieve before Void shows tickets Booked (1765766798599:Booked); FAIL Void succeeds (2xx, voided=true) (409 409 {"Status":409,"TransactionId":"3106b0a1-0366-4d41-b170-6e7c0cedcfe4","ErrorCode":"OperationNotSupported","ErrorMessa)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen upselling tier. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided; IDs unchanged from Hold.
Actual Result
Same as FLOW-V1-05 on the upsell fare: the chain works to ticketing and the ids are unchanged from Hold. V1 Upselling again lacks selectedOffer (upsellOffers[0] used), and the Void hop is refused as unsupported (ticket left live, voided via V2 in cleanup).

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen offer. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
All hops succeed before the hold expiry; BookAfterHold issues the ticket with unchanged ids; Void succeeds; the final Retrieve shows the cancelled state. Price reconciliation holds (1815 AED through PnrReprice and BookAfterHold). Note the V2 Hold date format carries a +02:00 offset (V1 uses Z).

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. Collection variables cleared. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling -> AddPassenger -> Book -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
Every hop succeeds with AddPassenger inserted; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result
The flow works with AddPassenger inserted and the booked price equals the Upselling tier (1815 AED, the only tier offered). Anomaly resolved: Book WITHOUT AddPassenger does not work on V2, it fails with an unhandled HTTP 500 (a 400 naming the missing passenger details would be expected). AddPassenger must follow Upselling.
FLOW-V2-76-TPN - [Search]&[UpSelling]&[AddPassenger]&[Hold]&[BookAfterHold]&[Void] [Response] Verify Family-E flow #76 completes end to end for TravelportNdc.PASS
Endpoint Name: Whole V2 upsell, hold and ticket flow ending in a void
Request: Upsold, added the passenger, held, repriced, ticketed from the hold and voided
Response: Every step worked and the booking reads as cancelled at the end
Expected: Every step works and the final lookup shows the ticket voided
Actual: Passed
Status: PASS

Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. canBeHeld=true on the chosen upselling tier. Run on one calendar day.
Steps
  1. Search -> UpSelling -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve -> Void -> Retrieve (post-Void check)
Expected Result
All hops succeed before holdExpirationDate; Void succeeds; final Retrieve shows all tickets voided.
Actual Result

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. A second ticketed TravelportNdc booking exists to supply the foreign token.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V1-03-TPN through hop 4 (Retrieve). At hop 5 replace bookingToken with the one from another booking. Retrieve both bookings afterwards.
Expected Result
Void rejected with a 4xx standard envelope; the flow's booking stays ticketed.
Actual Result
The Void is refused, both bookings stay ticketed, but only because V1 Void is unsupported for TravelportNdc: the stale-token check itself is never reached, so the check cannot be assessed on V1 (the V2 equivalent, NEGHOP6, shows the token is ignored). Blocked by TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03.
FLOW-V2-27-TPN-NEGHOP6 - [Search]&[FareConfirm]&[AddPassenger]&[Book]&[Retrieve]&[Void] [Request] Validate Family-C flow #27 rejects a stale bookingToken at the Void hop for TravelportNdc.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Void with another booking's token, V2 flow
Request: Booked a ticket, then asked for the void with a token from a different booking
Response: The void was accepted and the ticket voided
Expected: The void should be refused and the booking left ticketed
Actual: Failed: the wrong token was accepted
Status: FAIL
Evidence
ok Search offer reconciles (fully itemized offer picked) (28 of 53 offers fully itemized); ok FareConfirm reconciles; ok FareConfirm total equals Search total (1985 vs 1985); ok Book selectedOffer reconciles; ok Book total equals FareConfirm tier total (1985 vs 1985); FAIL Retrieve before Void shows tickets Booked (none); ok Void succeeds (2xx, voided=true) (200 200 {"voided":true,"voidedTickets":[{"ticketStatus":"Voided","ticketNumber":"1765766802060","carrierCode":"EK"}],"passen)

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-01 and TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03 passed. Staging only. A second ticketed TravelportNdc booking exists to supply the foreign token.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V2-27-TPN through hop 5 (Retrieve). At hop 6 replace bookingToken with the one from another booking. Retrieve both bookings afterwards.
Expected Result
Void rejected with a 4xx standard envelope; the flow's booking stays ticketed.
Actual Result
The stale token is not detected: Void succeeds with another booking's bookingToken and voids the flow's own booking (the donor booking stayed ticketed). Expected a 4xx and the booking left ticketed. Same root cause as VAL-02 / NEG-02. Side observation: Retrieve straight after an Emirates Book can return a retryable supplier error mapped to the unmapped NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999.
Findings12Defects7Unknown-resolution
Defect
TravelportNdc Book and Retrieve omit voidCapability on V1 and V2, even for a booking ticketed today (§2.9 voidCapability; §2.11; §4.7, TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-02)
Field: voidCapability
Expected value: "voidCapability": "<void-allowed value>" (e.g. FullVoidOnlyAllowed) on a same-day ticketed booking, switching to VoidNotAllowed once voided or past the window
Impact: Callers cannot decide from the booking whether to offer Void; the flag-vs-outcome consistency check (TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-05) cannot be performed
Evidence: V1 Book 72HIJQ and V2 Book 72HZA2 (2026-10-26): key lists contain no voidCapability; same for RetrieveBooking/Retrieve. Same defect as TravelportNdc V1 Book on 2026-08-05 and SabreNdc 2026-10-22/25
Defect
V1 Void for TravelportNdc is still rejected as 409 OperationNotSupported ("TravelportNdc does not exists") while V2 Void works on the same build (§2.15; AC Void Request, TC-CAPCHECK-TPN-03)
Field: ErrorCode / Context
Expected value: HTTP 200 {voided:true, voidedTickets:[{ticketStatus:"Voided", ticketNumber, carrierCode}]} for a same-day ticketed V1 booking, as V2 returns
Impact: V1 clients cannot void TravelportNdc bookings at all; every V1 Void case and V1 Void flow ends at the Void hop and the ticket stays live
Evidence: V1 72HIJQ Void 409 twice (TransactionIds fc7546a6-..., fb13b0d5-...); V2 72HZA2 Void 200 in 13.1s; build ndc-integration-stg-ne-5, 2026-10-26
Defect
TravelportNdc V2 Void ignores bookingToken: omitted, empty, whitespace-only, upper-cased, 1000-character or another booking's token all still void the booking (AC Error Handling; §2.15, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-02)
Field: bookingToken
Expected value: 400 standard envelope, e.g. {Status:400, ErrorCode:"NDC-INT-TEC-A0001", Context:[{Name:"PredicateValidator", Value:"BookingToken is required"}]}, booking left ticketed (a token that does not belong to the PNR rejected the same way)
Impact: The only secret proving the caller owns a booking is not checked; anyone who knows a gdsPNR can void that ticket (the PNR itself is not checked either, see BND-01)
Evidence: V2 72IAMX (token omitted) and 72IEZ9 (token empty) voided 2026-10-26; same behaviour for whitespace, upper-case, 1000-char and foreign tokens (BND-01, NEG-02)
Defect
TravelportNdc V2 Void ignores surName: a surname that matches no passenger, or no surname, voids the booking (same defect as SabreNdc 2026-10-22) (§2.15 Common Errors; AC Business Rules, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-04)
Field: surName
Expected value: 4xx standard envelope, e.g. {Status:400, ErrorCode:"NDC-INT-TEC-A0001", Context:[{Value:"surName does not match any passenger on the PNR"}]}, booking left ticketed
Impact: The documented passenger-identity check on Void is missing; a caller with a gdsPNR can void any ticketed booking (also lets every SEC-04 injection string through)
Evidence: V2 72J5K8 (surName Mismatch) and 72IQPE (surName omitted) voided 2026-10-26
Defect
TravelportNdc Void errors expose internal .NET type names (400 context) and the raw Travelport request/response (409 OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse) (AC Result Mapping; AC Error Handling; §2.9 Expected Failure (DTO leak defect); §7.14, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-07)
Field: context[].value / OriginalSupplierRequest / OriginalSupplierResponse
Expected value: context [{name:"voidTickets[0]", value:"Each voidTickets item must be an object with ticketNumber"}] and no OriginalSupplier* fields (or null)
Impact: Internal type names and supplier payloads are visible to API callers; raw supplier replies can contain record data and make error handling brittle
Evidence: V2 400 (voidTickets [123]) context names NDC.Integrations.Application.Dtos.Api.SharedTypes.TicketType; V2 409s for unknown PNR (ZZZZZZ), cancelled hold, and EGY-credential Void carry OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse; 2026-10-26
Defect
V2 Void returns passengersVoidedAncillaries: null for a booking without ancillaries; emdTickets is {} and SabreNdc returns {} for both (§2.15; §6.4 ANC, TC-VOIDTPN-VAL-10)
Field: passengersVoidedAncillaries
Expected value: "passengersVoidedAncillaries": {} (empty, as emdTickets and the SabreNdc response)
Impact: Clients that iterate the field without a null check fail on every TravelportNdc V2 Void; the two V2-only fields behave differently from each other
Evidence: V2 Void of 72HZA2: passengersVoidedAncillaries null, emdTickets {}; SabreNdc V2 Void SFDJFF: {} and {}, 2026-10-26
Defect
TravelportNdc V2 Void accepts a whitespace-only pnr (only non-empty and max 9 characters are checked) and voids the booking identified by gdsPNR (§2.15; §8 string-field boundary angle, TC-VOIDTPN-BND-01)
Field: pnr
Expected value: 400 standard envelope naming pnr for a blank value, e.g. Context [{Value:"PNR is required"}]
Impact: pnr is effectively decorative: a Void succeeds with a blank pnr, so the PNR/gdsPNR pair is never cross-checked and a mistyped pnr cannot be detected
Evidence: V2 72H7ZT voided with pnr ' ' on 2026-10-26; ErrorCode would be NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 as for an empty pnr
Defect
Void on a held, unticketed TravelportNdc booking returns 200 {voided:false, voidedTickets:[]} and cancels the hold (AC Void Request (eligible booking); §2.10; §2.14; §2.15, TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-03)
Field: voided
Expected value: A 4xx standard envelope, e.g. {Status:409, ErrorCode:"VoidNotEligible", ErrorMessage:"Only ticketed bookings can be voided"}, and the hold left alive
Impact: A caller that voids the wrong (held) booking silently loses the hold while receiving a 2xx; the response contradicts itself (success status, voided:false)
Evidence: V2 hold 72JHGP: Void 200 voided:false in 9.2s, then Retrieve 409 "Reservation is already cancelled", 2026-10-26
Defect
TravelportNdc V2 Void ignores the voidTickets list: a subset, a fabricated ticket number and another booking's ticket number all result in void-all of the PNR (same defect class as SabreNdc 2026-10-22) (§2.15 voidTickets; AC Business Rules, TC-VOIDTPN-BIZ-06)
Field: voidTickets
Expected value: Only the listed ticket voided (voidedTickets with one entry), or a 4xx envelope e.g. {Status:400, Context:[{Value:"Partial void is not supported"}]}; a ticket not on the PNR always rejected
Impact: Selective void silently becomes void-all: a caller asking to void one ticket loses every ticket, including a lone infant/adult pairing
Evidence: V2 72HKTY: voidTickets [1572141427292] voided all 3 tickets, 2026-10-26; see also NEG-03
Defect
Void for an unknown TravelportNdc record locator returns the unmapped 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (ErrorMessage = the code) and echoes the raw Travelport request and response (AC Error Handling; §2.15; §7.9, TC-VOIDTPN-NEG-01)
Field: ErrorCode / OriginalSupplierResponse
Expected value: {Status:404 or 409, ErrorCode:"BookingNotFound", ErrorMessage:"No booking found for the supplied PNR", Context:[...]} with no OriginalSupplier* content
Impact: Callers get no usable error code and supplier internals are exposed in the API response
Evidence: V2 TransactionId 56c05e57-6eb4-4b07-99b1-1901ddd1439d, 2026-10-26; same family as SabreNdc 2026-10-22
Defect
Void errors use two envelope casings (Status/ErrorCode vs status/errorCode "1001"), the unmapped NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 whose message equals the code, and two different codes for "reservation cancelled" depending on the carrier (QR BYP-A0003, EK Z9999) (AC Error Handling; AC Result Mapping; §2.9 Expected Failure, TC-VOIDTPN-NEG-05)
Field: error envelope (ErrorCode / ErrorMessage)
Expected value: {Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context} everywhere, one code for "already cancelled", distinct Void business-rule codes, a human-readable ErrorMessage on every error
Impact: Clients need two error parsers and cannot reliably detect the cancelled state (INT-02) or a not-found booking
